questions.sample_answer: I'd start with a golden set: around 50 real user questions with reference answers and the documents that should be retrieved. For each pipeline change I'd measure retrieval and generation separately. Retrieval with recall at 5, because if the right chunk isn't retrieved, the model can't answer. Generation with faithfulness, meaning every claim is supported by the retrieved context, scored by an LLM judge with a fixed rubric that I validated against my own ratings on 30 answers. I'd run this in CI, so a prompt or chunking change that drops recall or faithfulness by more than a couple of points fails the build. In my support-bot project that would have caught the time we changed the embedding model and recall quietly dropped.

questions.sample_answer: In my document-QA agent the state is a TypedDict with the question, retrieved chunks, a messages list and an error count. Each node returns only the keys it changes, and the messages list uses an add reducer so nodes append instead of overwriting. After the tool node, a conditional edge checks the error count: under three it loops back to retry with a rewritten query, otherwise it goes to a fallback answer. I compiled it with a checkpointer, so a crashed run can resume from the last completed step.
